 Abu Dhabi, 26 October (H.S.): 
 New The Abu Dhabi T10 League has taken a major step towards expanding its reach across the Indian subcontinent, with organisers awarding the broadcast rights for the 2026 season to JioStar. Under the agreement, all 32 matches will be telecast live on the Star Sports television network and streamed digitally on JioHotstar.
 According to the organisers, the partnership aims to broaden the tournament’s reach in India, one of the world’s largest cricket markets, and introduce more fans to the fast-paced T10 format. The agreement with JioStar forms an important part of the league’s wider global expansion strategy.
 The 2026 edition of the Abu Dhabi T10 will be held from November 7 to 20 at Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi. The tournament will feature 32 matches over 13 playing days, with three matches scheduled on six days and two matches on each of the remaining seven days.
 The official player draft was held in Abu Dhabi on September 30, with several prominent international cricketers expected to participate in the competition.
 Matt Boucher, chief executive officer of Abu Dhabi Cricket and Sports Hub and Abu Dhabi T10, said India had traditionally been the tournament’s largest and most enthusiastic market. He said the partnership with JioStar would enable the league to connect with a wider audience across India and the subcontinent.
 Boucher added that expanding the tournament’s broadcasting network was central to its long-term growth strategy. The organisers aim to establish Abu Dhabi T10 as a leading global sporting and entertainment property while strengthening its relationship with existing supporters and attracting new fans.
 Prashant Khanna, head of sports rights and innovation at JioStar, said the fast-paced T10 format had found an audience in India. He expressed confidence that JioStar’s extensive broadcasting and digital reach would help the tournament connect with cricket fans across the country.
 Beyond live match coverage, JioStar will support the tournament with initiatives designed to enhance fan engagement. These are expected to include exclusive content, behind-the-scenes access to players and digital features that bring supporters closer to the action throughout the competition.
 According to figures cited by the organisers, the 2025 edition generated more than 527 million social media impressions and recorded a broadcast media value of US$512 million. The new broadcasting partnership is expected to help increase viewership and audience engagement during the 2026 season.
 The tournament’s expansion strategy has gained further momentum following Abu Dhabi Cricket and Sports Hub’s assumption of majority ownership and commercial rights earlier this year.
 The organisers said institutional support, the participation of leading international players and a broader broadcasting network would be central to their efforts to establish Abu Dhabi T10 among the world’s prominent cricket events.
 With all 32 matches set to be available through Star Sports and JioHotstar in India, the partnership is expected to strengthen the tournament’s visibility in a key cricket market and support its ambitions for sustained international growth.
